tasks.short: Use search patterns to improve page targeting, content and visibility.

steps.what: Export query, impression, click and position data from {OTHER} search-performance reporting.
Export page engagement and conversion data from {OTHER} web analytics.
Join exports and compare page trends in {SPREADSHEET}.
Group queries by intent and document page mismatches in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Query text, page content and a fixed intent taxonomy.
loop.output: Query groups, supporting examples and uncertain page matches.
loop.check: Validate query coverage and page identifiers; the strategist reviews ambiguous and high-impact groups.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one repair pass per batch; unresolved groups enter a review queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Exact matching cannot reliably distinguish intent across varied query wording.

steps.what: Choose target pages and changes against business priorities.
Revise headings, metadata, copy and internal links in {CMS}.

loop.input: Approved change brief, existing copy, approved claims and allowed link targets.
loop.output: A page draft with a field-level change summary.
loop.check: Check field limits, links and protected fields; the editor checks accuracy, usefulness and tone.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per page; unsupported claims or unresolved ambiguity return to the editor.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle field structure but cannot write useful page-specific prose.

steps.what: Approve and publish the page changes in {CMS}.
Check post-publication trends and flag regressions in {BI}.

tasks.design: Scheduled integrations load aggregate search and website metrics from {OTHER} into {DATA_PLATFORM}, reconcile page identifiers and feed {BI}. Bounded loops propose intent groups and page drafts in {DOCS} and {CMS}; the strategist chooses changes and the editor approves publication. Deterministic monitoring links results to the publication log without claiming causation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Page identifiers, exports and content versions were fragmented. Maintaining joins and page-specific drafting logic cost more than periodic manual analysis.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing APIs, reusable data checks and faster AI-assisted connector development reduce build effort. Bounded text classification and drafting can handle varied queries and page copy.
tasks.still_hard: Search data is incomplete and delayed. Seasonality, competitor changes and ranking changes make causal attribution difficult; useful content still needs subject knowledge.
tasks.human_edge: Choose which audience needs deserve investment and balance search demand against usefulness, brand promises and commercial priorities.

ambition.what: Weekly page-investment decisions by query-intent group.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling exports and rewriting routine fields to choosing page experiments and reviewing results. The strategist gains delegated authority to prioritise changes within an agreed content budget; publication remains with the editor.

reach.task: Turn a query-intent brief into an accurate page revision.
reach.learn: Editorial standards, source verification and how to preserve reader value.

reach.task: Test whether query groups reflect unmet audience needs.
reach.learn: Sampling limits, customer research and alternatives to interpreting clicks as intent.

evidence.claim: Scheduled data joins, page comparisons and rule-based monitoring are deterministic engineering patterns; no search-specific case is supplied.
Shopify Sidekick supports product-description drafting; this supports a bounded copy-drafting component, not search-ranking gains.

assumptions: The baseline is a mid-size company with search reporting, web analytics, a {CMS} and occasional {SPREADSHEET} joins.
The structured-input prior supports automated preparation; the judgement prior supports retaining targeting decisions.
Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Build ranges cover one site and language with aggregate data. GDPR and EU AI Act requirements are assessed for the actual use; national rules govern any relevant employee consultation.
No visitor-level profiling or employee monitoring is introduced.
unknowns: Available API access, query suppression and historical data retention.
Whether page identifiers remain stable across reporting sources and {CMS} versions.
Actual editorial approval rights, languages and regulated claims.
Whether consultation under national rules applies to the proposed deployment.
research_questions: Which observation windows best separate normal search variation from meaningful regressions?
How should ambiguous queries and multi-intent pages be evaluated before expanding coverage?
new_work: Review ambiguous intent groups and unsupported copy.
Maintain page mappings, protected fields and approved claim sources.
Investigate regression alerts and record concurrent site or campaign changes.
Monitor connector failures and changes in source data definitions.

tasks.short: Coordinate technical website changes that improve search discovery and indexing.

steps.what: Inspect crawl findings and indexing errors in {OTHER} website diagnostics.
Write reproducible issues and acceptance criteria in {PROJECT}.

loop.input: Validated diagnostic findings, affected URLs and an acceptance-criteria template.
loop.output: A ticket with reproduction steps, evidence and proposed acceptance checks.
loop.check: Require evidence references and valid URLs; the strategist checks scope and removes unsupported diagnoses.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair per issue group; incomplete evidence returns to the strategist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates populate known errors, but site-specific explanations require reading diagnostic context.

steps.what: Assess causes and implementation risks in {OTHER} code and hosting tools.
Agree priority, scope and release timing with developers.
Chase progress and relay delivery updates through {EMAIL}.
Review checks and approve release in {OTHER} deployment tooling.
Recheck affected URLs in {OTHER} website diagnostics after release.

tasks.design: Configure {OTHER} website diagnostics to supply reproducible findings, then use a bounded drafting loop to prepare evidence-linked tickets in {PROJECT}. Shared status in {PROJECT} removes routine chasing, while deterministic checks compare affected pages before and after releases. Developers retain diagnosis, scope negotiation and approval of production changes in {OTHER} deployment tooling.
tasks.previous_blocker: Diagnostic output was disconnected from delivery tickets and release records. Turning findings into clear developer requests required repeated explanation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing diagnostic exports and delivery APIs support a small integration. AI-assisted development lowers its implementation cost, and bounded drafting reduces ticket preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Architecture trade-offs, undocumented dependencies and release capacity remain site-specific. Passing crawl checks does not establish business impact or guarantee indexing.
tasks.human_edge: Build agreement between marketing and development when search benefit competes with reliability, accessibility and delivery commitments.

ambition.what: Search impact assessment for planned website releases.

tasks.altitude: The strategist spends less time rewriting findings and chasing status, and more time shaping changes before development starts. An agreed release checklist gives the strategist a formal recommendation on search readiness; deployment authority stays with the development lead.

reach.task: Review navigation and page templates before implementation.
reach.learn: Information architecture, accessibility and rendering constraints.

reach.task: Compare technical search work with other marketing investments.
reach.learn: Opportunity cost, delivery capacity and uncertainty in benefit estimates.

evidence.claim: Crawl checks, ticket templates, shared delivery status and release validation can use existing configuration and deterministic integrations.
Site-specific diagnosis and cross-team priority negotiation remain judgement-heavy; the digest supplies no technical search coordination case.

assumptions: This task covers coordination and release review; implementation effort belongs to the developer's delivery task.
The baseline uses {PROJECT} for tickets and {EMAIL} for some status chasing.
The communication prior includes substantive technical discussion; only routine chasing disappears.
Time shares include participating roles within this coordination task and are estimates.
Build ranges cover one website and delivery workflow. GDPR, the EU AI Act and applicable national rules are assessed without introducing employee performance monitoring.
unknowns: Existing diagnostic capabilities and access to release events.
Whether deployment tooling supports required checks and rollback records.
Who can agree scope, approve production changes and accept search risks.
Whether access or employee consultation under national rules adds lead time.
research_questions: Which diagnostic checks reliably predict release regressions for this website architecture?
How should search readiness be assessed when rendering or indexing results arrive after release?
new_work: Maintain issue templates and acceptance checks.
Review drafted tickets for unsupported causes and duplicated issues.
Investigate failed release checks and assign follow-up work.
Maintain diagnostic credentials and connections to release records.

tasks.short: Set up reliable, privacy-aware measurement of website behaviour.

steps.what: Agree business questions, events and conversion definitions with the marketing manager.
Inspect existing events and tags in {OTHER} analytics and tag-management tooling.
Review collection purposes, consent conditions and retention in {DOCS}.
Configure events and triggers in {OTHER} tag-management tooling.
Test event payloads, duplicate firing and consent states using {OTHER} browser-testing tools.
Review test evidence and publish changes in {OTHER} tag-management tooling.
Check live event volumes and conversion continuity in {BI}.

tasks.design: A versioned measurement plan in {DOCS} drives deterministic inventory checks and configuration generation for {OTHER} tag-management tooling. Automated browser tests check payload schemas, duplicates and permitted collection under different consent states before a developer approves publication. Aggregate health checks in {DATA_PLATFORM} feed {BI} and route failures through {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Event specifications, consent conditions and implementation details were maintained separately. Manual browser checks were repeated after each change.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned schemas, reusable event templates and automated browser tests are established techniques. AI-assisted coding makes site-specific configuration adapters and test journeys cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Custom application events may require developer work. Consent choices, blocked collection and cross-device behaviour leave legitimate measurement gaps; privacy decisions cannot be inferred from technical checks.
tasks.human_edge: Decide what is worth measuring and whether the resulting evidence is useful and proportionate to the collection involved.

ambition.what: Measurement readiness review before a campaign launch.

tasks.altitude: The strategist spends less time clicking through test journeys and more time agreeing measurement quality before launch. The role gains authority to recommend measurement readiness; privacy approval and production publication retain their named owners.

reach.task: Validate whether behavioural events answer the intended business question.
reach.learn: Construct validity, selection bias and the limits of observed behaviour.

reach.task: Specify observable completion points in website journeys.
reach.learn: Interaction states, accessible journeys and stable event semantics.

evidence.claim: Schema-driven configuration, consent-state tests and event-volume checks can be deterministic; no model loop is required for the scoped implementation.
GDPR and applicable national rules require a deployment-specific privacy assessment; the digest supplies no website analytics implementation case.

assumptions: The baseline concerns a new measurement setup or material change; minor changes reuse an approved measurement plan.
The website has stable event hooks and templates for the first implementation scope. Unsupported custom events enter a developer exception queue.
The structured-input and low model-needed priors support a fully deterministic build around human measurement and privacy decisions.
Build ranges cover one website, one consent configuration and agreed test journeys; estimates include access and privacy review.

GDPR, national cookie rules and the EU AI Act are assessed as applicable. The access range allows consultation under national rules where employee monitoring is implicated; a longer formal process can extend it.
unknowns: Current collection purposes, lawful basis, consent design and retention settings.
Whether identifiers or sensitive information appear in event payloads.
Available test environments, event hooks and configuration APIs.
Whether employee-facing pages are included and consultation under national rules is required.
research_questions: Which test journeys provide adequate coverage of asynchronous and single-page navigation?
Which volume checks detect collection failures without treating consent-driven gaps as defects?
new_work: Maintain the event schema and test journeys when the website changes.
Review custom-event exceptions and proposed new collection purposes.
Investigate payload leaks, duplicate events and consent-state failures.
Update privacy documentation and access permissions when scope changes.

tasks.short: Agree campaign KPIs and produce reliable performance reports.

steps.what: Clarify campaign objectives and the decisions the report must support.
Define metrics, denominators, attribution windows and segments in {DOCS}.
Approve KPI definitions, targets and reporting caveats in {DOCS}.
Export campaign spend, clicks and attributed conversions from {ADS}.
Export qualified leads and recorded outcomes from {CRM}.
Reconcile sources and calculate the campaign scorecard in {SPREADSHEET}.
Write and check performance commentary in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Validated scorecard, quality flags, campaign change log and fixed reporting sections.
loop.output: A draft narrative with metric references, caveats and clearly labelled hypotheses.
loop.check: Recompute quoted figures and require source references; the strategist checks interpretation and causal language.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair per report; failed numerical checks fall back to a factual scorecard.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates can state movements, but explaining their relevance requires reading campaign context.

steps.what: Send the approved report to internal stakeholders through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Approved metric definitions in {DOCS} drive scheduled extraction from {ADS} and {CRM}, with reconciliation and calculations in {DATA_PLATFORM} feeding {BI}. A bounded loop drafts commentary from checked figures and a campaign change log, and the strategist approves its interpretation. Configured delivery through {EMAIL} distributes the approved report to an authorised internal list.
tasks.previous_blocker: Campaign identifiers, attribution windows and lead definitions differed across sources. Report production depended on manual reconciliation and repeated commentary writing.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned metric definitions and deterministic checks can make calculations repeatable. AI-assisted coding reduces connector effort, while bounded drafting can use the checked scorecard without calculating metrics itself.
tasks.still_hard: Attribution is not incrementality. Delayed sales outcomes, missing identifiers and changing definitions can make a precise-looking scorecard misleading.
tasks.human_edge: Choose measures that support real business decisions, challenge misleading success claims and explain uncertainty to budget owners.

ambition.what: Weekly campaign experiment continuation decisions using qualified outcomes.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from rebuilding reports to investigating exceptions and proposing experiments. The strategist gains delegated authority to recommend continuation or redesign at weekly reviews; budget approval stays with the marketing manager.

reach.task: Compare campaign investment options using qualified outcomes.
reach.learn: Budget constraints, contribution economics and the limits of attribution.

reach.task: Design a test that separates campaign effect from background demand.
reach.learn: Control groups, statistical uncertainty and incrementality.

evidence.claim: Metric catalogues, scheduled extraction, reconciliations and dashboards are deterministic reporting patterns.
The digest documents a report containing non-existent sources, supporting explicit source and factual checks for generated commentary.
The supplied digest provides no campaign-reporting case or measured savings for this task.

assumptions: The baseline is a lead-generating company using {ADS} and {CRM}; another business model needs a different outcome source.
KPI selection is revisited for new campaigns or changed objectives; routine reporting reuses approved definitions.
The structured-data prior supports automated reporting, while the judgement prior argues for retaining KPI selection and interpretation.
Time shares describe the combined KPI-setting and reporting task. Routine reporting alone would have a higher automated share.
Build ranges cover one reporting model and a small source set. GDPR and EU AI Act requirements are assessed for the actual use, with national rules checked if employee monitoring is introduced.
Reports use aggregate outcomes and do not rank individual employees.
unknowns: Actual campaign mapping quality, source access and reporting latency.
Whether lead qualification and revenue outcomes are recorded consistently.
Approved attribution windows, metric owners and report recipients.
Data retention, privacy restrictions and any employee consultation required under national rules.
research_questions: Which leading indicators predict qualified outcomes without rewarding low-quality volume?
Which experiment designs can estimate incremental effect at the available campaign scale?
new_work: Resolve missing campaign mappings and late outcome records.
Maintain versioned metric definitions and reconciliation tolerances.
Review narrative claims, uncertainty and material data-quality flags.
Maintain connector permissions, recipient lists and delivery rules.

role.altitude: The role moves toward choosing search investments, defining trustworthy measurement and shaping website changes before release. Delegated rights can cover content prioritisation and experiment recommendations; editors, marketing managers, privacy leads and developers retain their respective approvals.
reach: Editor: turn audience intent into useful, substantiated content.
Web and digital interface designer: shape discoverable, accessible navigation and page structures.
Market research analyst: test audience assumptions and campaign incrementality.
Marketing manager: connect search opportunities to commercial priorities and investment decisions.
skills_to_grow: Technical search diagnostics and release acceptance criteria
role.ambitious_version: Run a search experimentation programme that connects audience needs, content changes, technical releases and qualified commercial outcomes. Offer measurement and search readiness reviews before launches, with explicit uncertainty and named approval rights.
